messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: Multiple imputation redux
parts:
Hi David,

I think the problem comes when you're extracting your data from mice. mice doesn't store a list of imputed data sets. Instead it stores a list of imputed values for those missing values. So when you specify "data=datami$im" in runMI you're not actually providing runMI with a list of imputed data frames but a list of imputed values (where each element of the list is a variable in the original data set, see ?mids for more details). To get complete data from mice you need to use the complete function in mice. I've included a bit of code below that we use to get a list of data frames from imputations in mice.

Hope this helps,

Alex

mice.imp <- NULL
  for(i in 1:m) {
mice.imp[[i]] <- complete(x=MiceObjectHere, action=i, include=FALSE) 
  }

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: Multiple imputation redux
parts:
Is this a saturated model? If so I think you've discovered a bug in the lmrr chi square code when df=0 (which we'll have fixed in the next release). If you set the chi argument to 'mr', 'mplus' or 'none' the error should disappear. This error also does not appear to impact parameter estimates.

Thanks,

Alex
